title: Briefing: Italy, South Africa, France, Serbia, Canada, Germany and Albania
script: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November fourth, and this is the Unowned briefing: the stories that matter, checked and graded. It's read by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our published timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means one source so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.
Here are the top stories.
Italy. Today: Rete degli Studenti Medi coordinator urges more school funding, warns staff cuts lower teaching quality.
South Africa. Today: South African Government says asylum seekers and refugees cannot vote on local election day.
France. Yesterday: Rennes unions keep march route despite ban, count 45 strike calls, CGT expects higher turnout.
Serbia. On Monday: Serbia's top prosecutor orders action on student complaints against police chief Kričak, who remains in custody.
Canada. On Monday: Nine British Columbia First Nations file court challenge; Ottawa offers 10% stake, cites consulting 110 communities.
Germany. On Monday: Education Minister Karin Prien says youth concerns 30‑city marches are legitimate, promises dialogue; SPD calls summit.
Albania. On Monday: Mayor Veliaj accuses Prime Minister Rama of ordering prison transfer; Justice Minister Gogu denies allegations.
India. No new developments since Sunday, November first.
Now the details.

Italy. Today: The national coordinator of the Rete degli Studenti Medi school-student network tells la Repubblica that the government should invest more in schools, and that fewer staff would lower the quality of teaching. Students say they are protesting for teachers as well as for themselves. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, la Repubblica, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: Turnout and outcome of the CGIL general strike called for November twentieth.

South Africa. Today: The South African Government said on X, on local-election day, that asylum seekers and refugees may not vote. Its graphics cite the Refugee Regulations, which it says bar them from political activity, and the Electoral Act, which it says limits voting to registered citizens aged 18 or over. That's the authority's own claim, from its official statement, and we grade it alleged until independent reporting backs it up. Coming up: The new asylum appointment system Home Affairs said would be in place by November tenth.

France. Yesterday, Tuesday, November third: Rennes unions say they will keep their route for the November fifth march despite a prefectural ban, and have counted 45 specific strike calls across sectors. Ouest-France reports that the CGT's Ille-et-Vilaine federation expects turnout to exceed the roughly 15,000 who marched on October thirty-first. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Ouest-France, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Also yesterday: France: unions say a nationwide strike on November fifth is shaping up to be large, with the CGT counting 1,140 strike notices across its organisations, Ouest-France reports. We grade that reported: so far only Ouest-France has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation. Coming up: Turnout and outcome of the unions' November fifth interprofessional strike and demonstration.

Serbia. On Monday, November second: Serbia's Supreme Public Prosecutor's Office orders the Belgrade prosecutors to act on student complaints against criminal police chief Marko Kričak over an August 2025 incident in a Government of Serbia garage, which had gone more than a year without result, Vreme reports. The paper says Kričak, detained on November first, was still in custody on November third. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Vreme, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: Formation of the new government and the choice of prime minister.

Canada. On Monday, November second: Nine British Columbia First Nations announce Federal Court applications to quash the Pacific Link national-interest designation, saying Ottawa did not adequately consult them. Ottawa says it consulted more than 110 Indigenous communities and will offer a minimum 10 per cent ownership stake, The Globe and Mail and the Vancouver Sun report; Cold Lake First Nation filed the first challenge in October. We grade that confirmed: independent outlets report it. Coming up: Whether binding Pathways carbon-storage agreements are signed by the November fifteenth target.

Germany. On Monday, November second: Germany's Education Minister Karin Prien calls the concerns of the young people who marched in more than 30 cities on October thirty-first "legitimate and extremely relevant" and promises more dialogue, and SPD politicians call for a national education summit; these are proposals, not policy changes so far, The Local reports. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, The Local Germany, and isn't yet confirmed by a second. Coming up: Gen Z regelt plans another countrywide protest on November fourteenth.

Albania. On Monday, November second: Albania's jailed Tirana mayor Erion Veliaj accuses Prime Minister Edi Rama of orchestrating his prison transfer, which the government denies. Veliaj, held in pre-trial detention on corruption charges he denies, also said Justice Minister Toni Gogu demanded he give up control of the city, Tirana Times reports; the claims, relayed in part by his lawyer, are unverified. We grade that disputed: the accounts conflict, and our timeline sets out both.
Also on our watch, with no new developments in recent days.

India. The latest report, from Sunday, November first: Tens of thousands join the INDIA opposition bloc's rally at New Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, led by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and backed by the Cockroach Janta Party, demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over a voter-list revision that removed more than 130 million names, AP and Reuters report. Our grade: confirmed, with independent reporting from Al Jazeera and AP.
We'll bring you updates on those as soon as they become available.
That's the Unowned briefing for Wednesday, November fourth. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com. Thanks for listening.
